items.question: What happens when the two triangles unite and unfold again?
premises: Two triangles unite and move toward a six-spoked state.
Even in the union of unfolding they return to absorption in that state.
items.inference: The unfolding process repeatedly forms a sixfold structure and then reabsorbs into its source.
uncertainties: The exact referent of ta is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: By the union of two triangles they move into a six-spoked state, and even in the union of unfolding they again become absorbed in that.

rows.gloss: arising in the unfolding of will
rows.grounds: arising in the unfolding of will

rows.gloss: is said also of that movement
rows.grounds: is said also of that movement

items.question: What stirring clearly manifests the form of the power of action?
premises: A mutual stirring arises in the unfolding of will.
This stirring clearly manifests the form of the power of action.
items.inference: The mutual stirring within the unfolding of will is the clear expression of kriya-shakti.
uncertainties: The phrase tadgaterapi is compressed and its exact syntactic link is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: The mutual stirring that arises in the unfolding of will clearly manifests the form of the power of action, and it is also said to belong to that movement.

rows.gloss: but are not the supreme and bliss
rows.grounds: but are not the supreme and bliss

items.question: How can the two powers appear distinct if the supreme and bliss are undivided?
premises: The two powers share the same nature and do not exist otherwise.
The supreme and bliss are by their own nature free from division.
items.inference: The apparent duality of the powers does not contradict the undivided nature of the supreme and bliss.
uncertainties: The verse poses an objection that is answered in the next verse.
items.plain_english: Those very two powers share that same nature and do not stand apart; yet the supreme and bliss are, by their own nature, free from division.

rows.gloss: lord of consciousness of unlimited nature
rows.grounds: lord of consciousness of unlimited nature

items.question: How can such variety exist within an undivided self?
premises: An objection asks how such variety can be held within the self.
The lord of consciousness is of unlimited nature.
items.inference: The answer begins from the unlimited nature of the lord of consciousness.
items.plain_english: How can they hold such great variety within their own self? Listen: this lord of consciousness is of unlimited nature.

rows.gloss: lord of dissolution and arising of endless varied powers
rows.grounds: lord of dissolution and arising of endless varied powers

items.question: What would follow if the great lord remained in only one form?
premises: The great lord governs the dissolution and arising of endless varied powers.
A hypothetical is posed in which he remains in a single form.
items.inference: The hypothesis of a single fixed form conflicts with his lordship over endless powers.
items.plain_english: If the great lord, master of the dissolution and arising of endless varied powers, were to remain in only one form—

rows.gloss: he would abandon that like a pot and so on
rows.grounds: he would abandon that like a pot and so on

items.question: Why cannot the great lord be confined to a single limited form?
premises: If confined to one form, he would lose great-lordship and consciousness.
Limited luminosity is the mark of the inert, like a pot.
items.inference: The great lord cannot be limited, because limitation belongs to inert things.
items.plain_english: He would abandon his great-lordship and his nature as consciousness, like a pot and other inert things; for limited luminosity is indeed the mark of the inert.

rows.gloss: surging from the great ocean of awareness
rows.grounds: surging from the great ocean of awareness

items.question: Why do the lord's powers arise as manifold expressions?
premises: Awareness is distinct from the inert because it cannot be measured.
The lord's own powers surge from the great ocean of awareness.
items.inference: Because awareness is immeasurable, its powers naturally arise as manifold surges.
items.plain_english: Awareness is distinct from the inert because it cannot be measured; therefore his own powers surge forth from the great ocean of awareness.

rows.gloss: the variety of their own mutual collision
rows.grounds: the variety of their own mutual collision

rows.gloss: the variety of their own mutual collision
rows.grounds: the variety of their own mutual collision

items.question: How do the powers of awareness appear as variety?
premises: The powers are like waves rising from the ocean of awareness.
Their mutual collision produces variety.
items.inference: The variety of manifestation arises from the mutual interplay of the powers.
items.plain_english: Like waves, they take on the variety of their own mutual collision; that mutual variety of the powers is their interplay with one another.

rows.gloss: where the three powers have become manifest
rows.grounds: where the three powers have become manifest

items.question: What is declared to be the clear body of the power of action?
premises: The mutual variety of the powers is the supreme expression of kriya-shakti.
This occurs in the fourteenth abode where the three powers are manifest.
items.inference: The manifest interplay of the three powers is the clear body of kriya-shakti.
uncertainties: The identity of the fourteenth abode is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: They declare this very mutual variety to be the supreme, clear body of the power of action, in this fourteenth abode where the three powers have become manifest.

items.question: How do the scriptures describe this threefold manifestation?
premises: The teacher in the earlier teaching spoke of trident-ness.
Teachers who see reality called this state stainless.
items.inference: The threefold manifestation is scripturally identified as the trident and as stainless.
uncertainties: The specific earlier teaching is not named beyond śrīpūrvaśāsana.
items.plain_english: Therefore the teacher declared its trident-nature in the revered earlier teaching, and teachers who see reality called this state stainless.

rows.gloss: the possessor of power is tinged
rows.grounds: the possessor of power is tinged

items.question: Why is the possessor of power called stainless rather than the powers themselves?
premises: The possessor of power is not tinged by anything.
Will, knowledge, and action are tinged separately.
items.inference: Stainlessness belongs to the possessor of power, not to the separately appearing powers.
items.plain_english: The possessor of power is not tinged by anything, but will, knowledge, and action are tinged separately.

rows.gloss: by the possessor of power's own
rows.grounds: by the possessor of power's own

items.question: When does the triad of powers appear in its unified form?
premises: The triad is tinged when appearing separately through the possessor's modes.
The same triad can shine forth in unity.
items.inference: The three powers are distinct in operation but can appear as a single unified radiance.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of iṣyamāṇādikaiḥ is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: That same triad appears clearly through the possessor of power's own freely willed modes; but when it shines forth in unity, then—

items.question: How does immersion in the unified triad make the yogin stainless?
premises: In unity the triad cannot be qualified by anything because its modes cancel mutual limitation.
The vibrating triad of powers is the trident.
items.inference: By immersion in the unified trident of powers, the yogin becomes stainless.
items.plain_english: Then it cannot be qualified by anything, because its modes mutually cancel limitation; thus the vibrating triad of powers is the trident, and by quickly entering into it the yogin becomes stainless.

rows.grounds: through division into Brahmi and other forms reaches eight groups of eight

items.question: How does the eightfold structure expand into a larger system?
premises: An eightfold group begins from the supreme nectar state.
Through division into Brahmi and other forms it becomes eight groups of eight.
items.inference: The emanation unfolds from one eightfold structure into a sixty-fourfold pattern.
uncertainties: The verse summarizes a structure whose details are developed elsewhere.
items.plain_english: Thus, beginning from the supreme nectar state, such an eightfold group, through division into Brahmi and other forms, clearly becomes eight groups of eight.

rows.gloss: through the stain of knowable limitation becomes bindu-form
rows.grounds: through the stain of knowable limitation becomes bindu-form

items.question: How does the supreme power take on the form of bindu?
premises: The supreme power makes her own body manifest.
Through the stain of knowable limitation she appears in the form of bindu.
items.inference: Bindu is the supreme power appearing under the limiting condition of knowability.
items.plain_english: Here the supreme power, even while making her own body manifest, becomes bindu-form through the stain of knowable limitation.

rows.gloss: in the abode of moon, sun, and fire
rows.grounds: in the abode of moon, sun, and fire

items.question: What is the supreme bindu in relation to moon, sun, and fire?
premises: When the power of action has arisen, moon, sun, and fire appear as its abode.
The undivided light present there is called the supreme bindu.
items.inference: The supreme bindu is the undivided light underlying the differentiated triad of moon, sun, and fire.
items.plain_english: When the power of action has arisen in the abode of moon, sun, and fire, the undivided light there is, for us, the supreme bindu.

items.question: How is bindu described in the teaching on the protection of reality?
premises: The supreme lord spoke of bindu in the teaching on the protection of reality.
Bindu is located within the heart-lotus and consists of human, power, and Shiva.
items.inference: Scripture presents bindu as an inner locus uniting the levels of human, power, and Shiva.
items.plain_english: And in the teaching on the protection of reality, the supreme lord said that it stands within the circle of the heart-lotus and consists of human, power, and Shiva.

items.question: How should bindu be understood in relation to sound and dissolution?
premises: Bindu is to be known through distinctions of dissolution as the pure deliverer.
The sound whose nature is nada is present in all living beings.
items.inference: Bindu is linked to the inner nada-sound that pervades all beings and functions as a pure deliverer.
items.plain_english: It should be known, through distinctions of dissolution, as bindu, the pure deliverer; that sound whose nature is nada is present in all living beings.

rows.gloss: by division into lower and higher
rows.grounds: by division into lower and higher

items.question: How does the inner sound abide despite apparent divisions and qualities?
premises: The sound abides without activity even when divided into lower and higher.
Qualities like soothing or sharpness and colors like white or red appear as variety.
items.inference: The underlying sound remains inactive in itself while supporting varied experiential qualities.
items.plain_english: Divided into lower and higher, it still abides without activity; whatever variety appears as soothing or sharpness, white or red, and so on—

rows.gloss: that light is independent of them
rows.grounds: that light is independent of them

items.question: What illuminates the light that underlies all qualities?
premises: That light is in itself independent of the varied qualities.
The teacher said that sun, moon, and fire do not illuminate it.
items.inference: The foundational light is not illuminated by any external luminary.
items.plain_english: That light is in itself independent of them; and the teacher said that neither sun, nor moon, nor fire illuminates it.

rows.gloss: and of sun, moon, and fire
rows.grounds: and of sun, moon, and fire

items.question: Do sun, moon, and fire have any light of their own?
premises: Sun, moon, and fire do not illuminate the foundational light.
Without that light they have no radiance of their own.
items.inference: All apparent luminosity depends on consciousness, which shines by itself.
items.plain_english: Sun, moon, and fire have no radiance of their own apart from that light; rather, consciousness shines in this way.

rows.gloss: joined with varied limiting conditions arising from its own freedom
rows.grounds: joined with varied limiting conditions arising from its own freedom

rows.gloss: inner variety such as sharpness and so on
rows.grounds: inner variety such as sharpness and so on

items.question: Why does the one light appear with qualities like sharpness?
premises: The light remains fundamentally one.
Varied limiting conditions arise from its own freedom.
items.inference: The one light appears as inner variety because of freely arisen limiting conditions.
items.plain_english: Joined with varied limiting conditions that arise from its own freedom, the light takes on inner variety such as sharpness and other qualities.

items.question: How does a limiting condition change the experience of light?
premises: The sun is normally hard to look at.
When its light falls on water, it becomes pleasing to the eyes.
items.inference: A limiting condition can transform how the same light is experienced.
items.plain_english: Even the sun, though hard to look at, becomes a delight to the eyes when it falls on water; see the power of a limiting condition.

rows.gloss: that light is stained by limiting conditions
rows.grounds: that light is stained by limiting conditions

items.question: On what does the light in sun and other luminaries ultimately depend?
premises: The light seen in sun and other luminaries is conditioned by limiting factors.
Such conditioned light depends on the light of consciousness belonging to the great lord.
items.inference: All conditioned luminosity ultimately depends on the supreme light of consciousness.
items.plain_english: In the sun and other luminaries, that light is stained by limiting conditions and therefore depends on the light of consciousness belonging to the great lord.
